content: 1. Hypertension should be closely monitored when using ozanimod in combination with other medications. 2. The concurrent use of voclosporin and ozanimod may increase the effects of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. The combination of ozanimod and voriconazole can also prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 4. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs that have known arrhythmogenic properties. 5. The combination of ozanimod and vorinostat increases the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 6. Ozanimod decreases the efficacy of the yellow fever vaccine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Live-attenuated vaccines should not be used with ozanimod during treatment and for up to three months after discontinuation of ozanimod. 8. The combination of ozanimod and ziprasidone increases the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 9. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of zolmitriptan through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. The active metabolite of ozanimod inhibits MAO-B in vitro, which may lead to serious adverse reactions, including hypertensive crisis. Co-administration of ozanimod with drugs that increase norepinephrine or serotonin is not recommended. Monitor for hypertension with concurrent use. 11. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of transdermal zolmitriptan through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including increased blood pressure and heart rate. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Ozanimod decreases the efficacy of the live zoster vaccine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Live-attenuated vaccines should not be used with ozanimod during treatment and for up to three months after discontinuation of ozanimod. 14. Ozanimod decreases the efficacy of the recombinant zoster vaccine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. There is no clinical data available on the efficacy and safety of vaccinations in patients taking ozanimod. Vaccinations may be less effective if co-administered with ozanimod. 16. Data on the use of ozanimod in pregnant women is not available. Based on animal studies, ozanimod may cause fetal harm. 17. There is no data on the presence of ozanimod in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production. 18. Ozanimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P subtypes 1 (S1P1) and 5 (S1P5). It blocks lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes, reducing the number of lymphocytes in peripheral blood. 19. The mechanism by which ozanimod exerts its therapeutic effects in multiple sclerosis (MS) and ulcerative colitis (UC) is unknown but may involve the reduction of lymphocyte migration into the central nervous system and intestine. 20. Ozanimod reaches peak plasma concentration in 6-8 hours. 21. The volume of distribution (Vd) of ozanimod is 5590 L, with 27% of the drug being ozanimod itself. 22. Ozanimod is metabolized by multiple enzymes to form major active metabolites (e.g., CC112273, CC1084037) and several minor active metabolites (e.g., RP101988, RP101075, RP101509) with similar activity and selectivity for S1P1 and S1P5. 23. The active metabolite CC112273 is further metabolized by CYP2C8 to form RP101509 or reduced to form CC1084037. 24. Approximately 94% of the circulating total active drug exposure is represented by ozanimod (6%), CC112273 (73%), and CC1084037 (15%). 25. The clearance of ozanimod is 192 L/hr. 26. Ozanimod can be taken with or without food, but foods with high tyramine content (e.g., aged, fermented, cured, smoked, and pickled foods) should be avoided. 27. Capsules should be swallowed whole. 28. Store ozanimod at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F). 29.
